title: The Little Prince
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
description: 《小王子》是法国飞行员作家安托万·德·圣埃克苏佩里（Antoine de Saint-Exupéry）于 1943 年创作的世界级哲理童话。飞行员主角因飞机故障坠毁在撒哈拉沙漠，意外结识了来自远方 B-612 小行星的小王子。小王子讲述了他离开深爱的玫瑰花、穿梭于各个行星的奇妙旅程——他遇到了专制的国王、爱慕虚荣的人、借酒浇愁的酒鬼、忙碌计算的实业家以及忠诚的点灯人，最终在地球遇到了智慧的狐狸。狐狸教会了他“只有用心才能看得清，实质性的东西是眼睛看不见的”这一真谛。全书文笔清澈如水，蕴含深邃的人文关怀与哲学思考。

chapters.title: Chapter 1: The Boa Constrictor
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 1 章：吞象的巨蟒画作

paragraphs.en: Once when I was six years old I saw a magnificent picture in a book, called True Stories from Nature, about the primeval forest. It was a picture of a boa constrictor in the act of swallowing an animal. Here is a copy of the drawing.
paragraphs.zh: 在我六岁的时候，在一本描写原始森林的名叫《真实的故事》的书中，看到过一副精彩的插图。那是一幅巨蟒正在吞食野兽的图画。这是那幅画的复刻版。

paragraphs.en: In the book it said: "Boa constrictors swallow their prey whole, without chewing it. After that they are not able to move, and they sleep through the six months that they need for digestion."
paragraphs.zh: 书中写道：“巨蟒把猎物整个吞进肚子里，咀嚼都不咀嚼。然后它们就不能动弹了，要在长达六个月的睡眠中消化食物。”

paragraphs.en: I pondered deeply, then, over the adventures of the jungle. And after some work with a colored pencil I succeeded in making my first drawing. My Drawing Number One. It looked something like this:
paragraphs.zh: 当时，我对丛林里的冒险思想了很久。于是，我用彩色铅笔成功画出了我的第一幅画。我的第一号作品。它看起来像这样：

paragraphs.en: I showed my masterpiece to the grown-ups, and asked them whether the drawing frightened them.
paragraphs.zh: 我把我的杰作拿给大人看，问他们我的画是不是吓着他们了。

paragraphs.en: But they answered: "Frightened? Why should any one be frightened by a hat?"
paragraphs.zh: 可他们回答说：“吓人？一顶帽子有什么好吓人的？”

paragraphs.en: My drawing was not a picture of a hat. It was a picture of a boa constrictor digesting an elephant. But since the grown-ups were not able to understand it, I made another drawing: I drew the inside of a boa constrictor, so that the grown-ups could see it clearly. They always need to have things explained. My Drawing Number Two looked like this:
paragraphs.zh: 我的画画的不是一顶帽子。那是一条巨蟒在消化一只大象。但是大人们看不懂，所以我又画了另一幅：我画了巨蟒肚子里面的情形，好让大人能看得清清楚楚。他们总是需要解释。我的第二号作品是这样的：

paragraphs.en: The grown-ups' response, this time, was to advise me to lay aside my drawings of boa constrictors, whether from the inside or the outside, and devote myself instead to geography, history, arithmetic, and grammar. That is why, at the age of six, I gave up what might have been a magnificent career as a painter. I had been disheartened by the failure of my Drawing Number One and my Drawing Number Two. Grown-ups never understand anything by themselves, and it is tiresome for children to be always and forever explaining things to them.
paragraphs.zh: 大人们对这幅画的反应是，劝我把巨蟒的画——无论是外面的还是里面的——放在一边，把精力投到地理、历史、算术和语法上去。就这样，在六岁那年，我放弃了本可以成为伟大画家的光辉前途。我的第一号作品和第二号作品的失败让我灰了心。大人们自己什么也弄不懂，单要孩子们一遍又一遍地给他们作解释，真是太累人了。

chapters.title: Chapter 2: In the Sahara Desert
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 2 章：撒哈拉沙漠的相遇

paragraphs.en: So I lived my life alone, without anyone that I could really talk to, until I had an accident with my plane in the Desert of Sahara, six years ago. Something was broken in my engine. And as I had with me neither a mechanic nor any passengers, I set myself to attempt the difficult repair job, all alone. It was a question of life or death for me: I had scarcely enough drinking water to last a week.
paragraphs.zh: 就这样，我独自一人生活着，没有一个真正谈得来的人，直到六年前我的飞机在撒哈拉沙漠出了故障。我的发动机里有什么东西给卡住了。因为我既没带机械师，也没带乘客，我便一个人干起了这项艰难的维修工作。这对我来说是生死攸关的事：我带的饮用水只够维持一个星期的。

paragraphs.en: The first night, then, I went to sleep on the sand, a thousand miles from any inhabited territory. I was more isolated than a shipwrecked sailor on a raft in the middle of the ocean. Thus you can imagine my amazement, at sunrise, when I was awakened by an odd little voice. It said:
paragraphs.zh: 第一天晚上，我在离有人烟的地方一千英里的沙漠上睡着了。我比在茫茫大海中依靠木筏漂流的落难水手还要孤立无援。因此，当太阳升起时，我被一个奇异的小声音唤醒，你可以想象我是多么惊讶了。那个声音说：

paragraphs.en: "If you please—draw me a sheep!"
paragraphs.zh: “请……给我画一只羊吧！”

paragraphs.en: "What!"
paragraphs.zh: “什么！”

paragraphs.en: "Draw me a sheep..."
paragraphs.zh: “给我画一只羊……”

paragraphs.en: I jumped to my feet, completely thunderstruck. I blinked my eyes hard. I looked carefully all around me. And I saw a most extraordinary small person, who stood there examining me with great seriousness. Here you may see the best portrait that, later on, I was able to make of him.
paragraphs.zh: 我一跃而起，像被雷劈了一样。我用力眨了眨眼睛。仔细地看了看周围。我看到一个非常非凡的小人儿，站在那里非常严肃地审视着我。这里就是我后来能够为他画出的最好的一副肖像。

paragraphs.en: Now I stared at this sudden apparition with my eyes starting out of my head in astonishment. Remember, I had crashed in the desert a thousand miles from any inhabited region. And yet my little man did not seem to be straying in the desert, nor dying of fatigue, of hunger, of thirst, or of fear. He did not give the impression of a child lost in the middle of the desert, a thousand miles from any human habitation.
paragraphs.zh: 此时，我张大眼睛惊讶地看着这个突然显现的小人。别忘了，我当时正身处远离人烟千里的沙漠之中。可这个小家伙看起来既不像是在沙漠中迷了路，也不像是因为疲倦、饥饿、口渴或害怕而要死去的样子。他一点也不像一个在远离人烟千里的沙漠中央迷路的小孩。

paragraphs.en: When at last I was able to speak, I said to him: "But—what are you doing here?"
paragraphs.zh: 当我看终于能说出话来时，我对他说：“可是……你在干什么呢？”

paragraphs.en: And in answer he repeated, very slowly, as if he were speaking of a matter of great consequence: "If you please—draw me a sheep..."
paragraphs.zh: 作为回答，他非常缓慢地重复着，仿佛在说一件非常重大的事情：“请……给我画一只羊……”

chapters.title: Chapter 3: The Little Prince’s Planet
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 3 章：小王子的神秘星球

paragraphs.en: It took me a long time to learn where he came from. The little prince, who asked me so many questions, never seemed to hear the ones I asked him. It was from words dropped by chance that, little by little, everything was revealed to me.
paragraphs.zh: 我很长时间才明白他是从哪里来的。小王子问了我许多问题，却好像从来听不见我问他的问题。我是从他无意中吐露的字眼里，才一点一点了解了一切。

paragraphs.en: The first time he caught sight of my airplane, for instance (I shall not draw my airplane; that would be much too complicated for me), he asked:
paragraphs.zh: 比如，当他第一次看到我的飞机时（我不画我的飞机，那对我来说太复杂了），他问：

paragraphs.en: "What is that object?"
paragraphs.zh: “那是个什么东西？”

paragraphs.en: "That is not an object. It flies. It is an airplane. It is my airplane."
paragraphs.zh: “那不是个东西。它会飞。那是一架飞机。是我的飞机。”

paragraphs.en: And I was proud to have him learn that I could fly. He cried out then:
paragraphs.zh: 我很自豪地让他知道我会飞。这时他大声叫道：

paragraphs.en: "What! You dropped down from the sky?"
paragraphs.zh: “什么！你是从天上掉下来的？”

paragraphs.en: "Yes," I answered modestly.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我谦虚地回答。

paragraphs.en: "Oh! That is funny!"
paragraphs.zh: “啊！这真滑稽！”

paragraphs.en: And the little prince broke into a lovely peal of laughter, which irritated me. I like my misfortunes to be taken seriously. Then he added:
paragraphs.zh: 小王子发出一阵清脆愉悦的笑声，这让我有点恼火。我希望别人严肃对待我的不幸。接着他又补充道：

paragraphs.en: "So you, too, come from the sky! Which is your planet?"
paragraphs.zh: “这么说，你也是从天上来的！你是哪颗星球上的？”

paragraphs.en: At that moment I caught a gleam of light in the mystery of his presence, and I demanded abruptly: "Do you come from another planet, then?"
paragraphs.zh: 那一刻，我在他降临的谜团中捕捉到了一缕微光，我突然问道：“那么，你是从另一颗星球上来的吗？”

paragraphs.en: But he did not answer. He tossed his head gently, without taking his eyes from my plane: "It is true that on that thing you couldn't have come from very far away..." And he sank into a reverie, which lasted a long time. Then, taking my sheep out of his pocket, he buried himself in the contemplation of his treasure.
paragraphs.zh: 但他没有回答。他轻轻地摇了摇头，眼睛没有离开我的飞机：“确实，坐着这玩意儿，你不可能从很远的地方来……”接着他就陷入了长久的沉思。然后，他从口袋里掏出我画的羊，沉浸在对自己宝贝的凝视中。

chapters.title: Chapter 4: The Discovery of Asteroid B-612
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 4 章：发现 B-612 小行星

paragraphs.en: I had thus learned a second fact of great importance: this was that the planet the little prince came from was scarcely any larger than a house!
paragraphs.zh: 就这样，我了解到了第二个非常重要的事实：小王子来自的那个星球，几乎比一栋房子大不了多少！

paragraphs.en: But that did not really surprise me much. I knew very well that in addition to the great planets—such as the Earth, Jupiter, Mars, Venus—to which we have given names, there are also hundreds of others which are sometimes so small that it is very difficult to see them through the telescope.
paragraphs.zh: 但这并没有让我太感到吃紧。我很清楚，除了地球、木星、火星、金星这些我们已经给它们起了名字的大星球之外，还有成百上千颗其他的小行星，有时它们小得很难通过望远镜看到。

paragraphs.en: When an astronomer discovers one of these, he does not give it a name, but only a number. He calls it, for instance, "Asteroid 3251."
paragraphs.zh: 当天文学家发现其中一颗时，他不会给它起名字，而只给它一个编号。例如，他会称它为“第 3251 号小行星”。

paragraphs.en: I have serious reason to believe that the planet on which the little prince lived was the asteroid known as B-612. This asteroid has only once been seen through the telescope. That was by a Turkish astronomer, in 1909.
paragraphs.zh: 我有严肃的理由相信，小王子生活的那个星球就是人们所说的 B-612 小行星。这颗小行星只在 1909 年被一位土耳其天文学家通过望远镜看到过一次。

paragraphs.en: On making his discovery, the astronomer had presented it to the International Astronomical Congress, in a great demonstration. But he was in Turkish costume, and so nobody would believe what he said. Grown-ups are like that.
paragraphs.zh: 当时发现之后，天文学家在一次国际天文学大会上盛装展示了他的发现。 But 他穿着土耳其传统服装，所以没有人相信他所说的话。大人们就是这个样子。

paragraphs.en: Fortunately, however, for the reputation of Asteroid B-612, a Turkish dictator made a law that his people, under pain of death, should change to European costume. So in 1920 the astronomer gave his demonstration all over again, dressed with great elegance and refinement. And this time everybody accepted his report.
paragraphs.zh: 幸运的是，为了 B-612 小行星的声誉，一位土耳其独裁者立了一条法律，逼迫他的人民改穿欧洲服装，违者处以死刑。于是，在 1920 年，这位天文学家身穿非常优雅考究的西装，重新进行了他的报告。这一次，所有人都接受了他的报告。

chapters.title: Chapter 5: The Baobab Trees
chapters.chineseTitle: 第 5 章：可怕的猴面包树

paragraphs.en: As each day passed I would learn, in our talk, something about the little prince's planet, his departure from it, his journey. The information would come very quietly, as it might chance to fall from his thoughts. It was in this way that I heard, on the third day, about the catastrophe of the baobabs.
paragraphs.zh: 随着日子一天天过去，在我们的交谈中，我会了解到一些关于小王子的星球、他的离开以及他的旅程的事情。这些信息来得非常安静，就像是从他的心思里无意中散落出来的一样。就是通过这种方式，在第三天，我听说了猴面包树的灾难。

paragraphs.en: This time, once more, I had the sheep to thank for it. For the little prince asked me abruptly, as if seized by a grave doubt: "It is true, isn't it, that sheep eat little bushes?"
paragraphs.zh: 这一次，我又得感谢那只羊了。因为小王子突然问我，仿佛被一个严重的顾虑所困扰：“羊吃小灌木，这是真的，对吧？”

paragraphs.en: "Yes, that is true."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，那是真的。”

paragraphs.en: "Ah! I am glad!"
paragraphs.zh: “啊！我真高兴！”

paragraphs.en: I did not understand why it was so important that sheep should eat little bushes. But the little prince added: "Then it follows that they also eat baobabs?"
paragraphs.zh: 我不明白羊吃小灌木为什么会有这么重要。但小王子补充道：“那么，这也意味着它们也吃猴面包树啰？”

paragraphs.en: I pointed out to the little prince that baobabs were not little bushes, but, on the contrary, trees as big as castles; and that even if he took a whole herd of elephants with him, the herd would not eat up one single baobab.
paragraphs.zh: 我向小王子指出，猴面包树可不是小灌木，相反，它们是像城堡一样巨大的大树；就算他带上一整群大象，这群大象也吃不完一棵猴面包树。

paragraphs.en: The idea of the herd of elephants made the little prince laugh. "We should have to put them one on top of the other," he said.
paragraphs.zh: 大象群的想法让小王子笑了。“我们得把大象一只叠一只地摞起来，”他说。

paragraphs.en: But he remarked wisely: "Before they grow so big, the baobabs start out by being little."
paragraphs.zh: 但他聪明地备注道：“在猴面包树长得那么大之前，它们刚开始也是小小的。”

paragraphs.en: "That is strictly true," I said. "But why do you want your sheep to eat the little baobabs?"
paragraphs.zh: “那倒完全没错，”我说。“但是你为什么想让你的羊吃掉小猴面包树呢？”

paragraphs.en: He answered me at once, "Oh, come! Come!" as if he were speaking of something that was self-evident. And I was obliged to use a great effort of intelligence to solve this problem, all by myself.
paragraphs.zh: 他立刻回答我：“哎呀！来吧！这还用说吗！”仿佛他在说一件显而易见的事情。我费了很大的心思，才靠自己解开了这个难题。
